extracted.intended_audience: economists, patent scholars, IP policymakers, patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the quality of issued patents using a probabilistic frame that treats patents as rights with a measurable likelihood of surviving validity challenges, claim construction, and enforcement. The rubric emphasizes indicators observable from prosecution, specification, litigation/settlement behavior, and examination effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity Confidence is High
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent would likely survive a serious validity challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals include: prior art was thoroughly searched and addressed during prosecution; independent claims are clearly differentiated from cited art; specification clearly enables and describes the full claim scope; subject-matter eligibility is unambiguous. High validity confidence reduces the patent's probabilistic invalidity risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Confidence is High
rubrics_metrics.description: A reader can predict claim construction and the patent's scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for: claim terms explicitly defined or having settled meaning in the art; prosecution history showing consistent claim interpretation; absence of ambiguous functional language without 35 U.S.C. §112(f) treatment; means-plus-function elements with clear corresponding structure in the specification. High scope confidence makes enforcement and licensing outcomes more predictable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability Confidence is High
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent is unlikely to be defeated on enforceability grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant indicators: inventorship properly disclosed; no inequitable conduct red flags (e.g., undisclosed material art known to the applicant); continuation/divisional history that does not trigger obviousness-type double patenting; maintenance fees are current. These reduce risks of unenforceability defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation Pyramids (quality defect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long chains of continuations used to capture competitor products and expand claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation pyramids signal post-hoc claim drafting and are often vulnerable to written-description challenges. Presence of extensive continuation practice lowers probabilistic quality even if individual claims were granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional Claiming Without Structural Support (quality defect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims expressed in result-oriented or 'means for' language lacking corresponding structure in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such functional claiming (e.g., issues highlighted by Williamson v. Citrix) creates vulnerability under §112 and reduces scope confidence because the claim may lack adequate structural support for enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Mismatches (quality defect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issued claims that overlap substantially with prior art not considered during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When substantial prior art was not considered, the patent's validity probability is lower. Assess how much of the prior art universe was actually considered during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation Anomalies (quality signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner behavior in litigation that indicates weak underlying claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include shifting claim construction positions across cases. Such tactical litigation behavior signals weaknesses in scope or validity and reduces confidence in the patent's probabilistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and Licensing Signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns of settlement and licensing that provide information about patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation rules: quick low-value settlements may indicate the patentee knows the patent is weak; large settlements without trial may reflect either strong patents or nuisance-value pressure; repeat licensing across many defendants may suggest either scope clarity (high quality) or cost-of-litigation arbitrage (independent of quality). Use settlement patterns cautiously as noisy indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability patent survives a competent IPR petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Operative question: What is the realistic probability this patent survives a competent inter partes review (IPR) petition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate survival probability using examination record, prior art coverage, and known IPR outcomes for similar patents. A high survival probability signals high probabilistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability asserted claim construction holds at Markman
rubrics_metrics.description: Operative question: What is the realistic probability the asserted claim construction holds at Markman?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of claim terms, presence of explicit definitions, prosecution arguments, and intrinsic evidence that would constrain construction. Predictability of Markman outcomes relates directly to scope confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of prior art universe considered during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Operative question: How much of the prior art universe was actually considered during examination?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure thoroughness of search and examiner's treatment of cited references. Limited prior art consideration increases the patent's invalidity probability; broad, addressed prior art increases validity confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution history supports non-trivial scope versus perfunctory prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Operative question: Does the prosecution history support a non-trivial scope, or was prosecution perfunctory?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether claims were substantively negotiated and justified in view of art, or if grants appear routine/uncalled-for. Perfunctory prosecution reduces confidence in both scope and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-related vulnerabilities (intervening rights, written description, OTDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operative question: Are there continuation-related vulnerabilities such as intervening rights, written-description gaps, or obviousness-type double patenting (OTDP)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine family history for continuations/divisions that could create entitlement problems or allow challenges. Such vulnerabilities materially increase probabilistic invalidity or unenforceability risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core empirical litigation/invalidity rates (contextual metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are probabilistic rights supported by empirical facts: only a small fraction are litigated and a substantial share of tried patents are invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key statistics to keep in mind: roughly 1.5% of patents are litigated; 0.1% are litigated to trial; of those tried, ~46% are held invalid. These numbers justify using a probabilistic rather than absolute view of patent quality and valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthening Post-Grant Review (quality mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform proposal: make cheap administrative challenges available shortly after grant to improve overall patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant review mechanisms allow third parties to correct errors quickly and cheaply, lowering the ex ante probability of weak patents remaining enforced. This is a production-side mechanism rather than a single-patent scoring metric, but it affects how to evaluate issued patents in aggregate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing the Validity Presumption (quality mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform proposal: reduce the strong 'clear and convincing' validity presumption afforded to issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting a weaker presumption would align legal standards with probabilistic realities and change expected settlement dynamics; consider this when modeling litigation/settlement outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage Examination Resources Toward Commercially Significant Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform proposal: devote more examiner effort to patents where quality matters most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize examiner resources to high-value applications to improve overall societal allocation of examination effort; when evaluating a patent, consider whether it was likely to have received adequate examiner attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure / Public Access to File Histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform proposal: increase public access to file histories so third parties can assess validity probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent prosecution records help outside parties evaluate prior art consideration and prosecution choices, improving market assessments of probabilistic quality.
